When card #n is delegated to exactly one agent, the session sits at that agent's desk; delegated to none or to several, the card is linked (it shows on the tag) but the session keeps its own desk. When both the session and the card's project have repos, they must match.

`flow office bridge` sends `agentflow` for T3 threads with the runner's title.

### Repos on projects

To say which agents belong to a project, give the project its code repositories. In the Timeline's **Projects** panel, each project has a **Repos** field: a comma-separated list of names (`lantern`), owner and name (`acme/lantern`) or git remotes (`https://github.com/acme/lantern.git`, `git@github.com:acme/lantern.git`). Through the API or MCP, send `repos` to `projects.create` or `projects.update` (`[]` clears them).

Repos are compared without `.git`, the protocol and the host: owner and name when both sides have them (so someone's fork with the same name is not the project), otherwise the bare name.

```sh
flow projects update Lantern --repos acme/lantern,acme/lantern-site
```

### Report your agents: flow office bridge

`flow office bridge` runs on your own machine and keeps your agents in the office. Every 3 seconds it reads the agents running there and sends them as source `bridge:<hostname>`, and it waits for Allow / Deny answers and carries them out.

- **T3 Code.** It reads T3's state database (`~/.t3/userdata/statev2.sqlite`, read-only) for threads with a running turn: title, model, the project folder's git remote, latest activity, subagents, open approval requests and the last 12 lines of the conversation (user and assistant messages, one line per command, file edit or tool). Allow and Deny go through T3's own API (a short-lived token from `t3 auth session issue`), after checking that the request is still open. Top-level threads take **Send to agent** (`t3 thread send`, with the text on standard input) and **Stop** (T3's `run.interrupt`, for the same turn that was running), after checking the thread is still running there; threads delegated by another thread are steered by that thread. The bridge logs each message and stop with the agent and how it went, never the text. Questions are answered in T3.
- **Claude Code** in a terminal. Running sessions (`~/.claude/sessions/` and their transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`) are reported with their status, latest activity and the last 12 lines of the conversation. Their prompts cannot be answered from outside, and they cannot take messages or be stopped from the office, so they show without buttons (`can: []`). Sessions T3 runs are reported once, as T3 agents.

Open **AgentFlow › 3D › Connect your agents**. Choose the operating system on the machine that runs your agents, then create a bridge key. Copy the terminal commands or paste the setup prompt into a local coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. The dialog confirms the first report from a new source, even if no agents are running yet.

You can also give your coding agent this prompt and supply the server URL and a key when it asks.

```text
Connect my local coding agents to the Flow 3D office. Detect the operating system on this machine.

Ask me for my Flow server URL and have me create a dedicated API key in Settings › Connect. Choose the current environment and Read & write. Ask me to provide the key privately.

1. On this machine, install the Flow CLI with `npm install -g github:aribradshaw/flow` (requires Node.js 24 or newer and Git).
2. Use a dedicated XDG_CONFIG_HOME for the office bridge so my normal Flow CLI login is preserved. Sign in to the Flow server I provide using `flow login --url <server> --key-stdin` and pass the key privately on stdin. Keep the key in the CLI config only. Never write it into a repo, command arguments, a service definition, logs or shell history. Don't print it again.
3. In the same configuration, run `flow office bridge --once --dry-run`. Show me what the bridge would send and wait for my approval before sending a report.
4. Set up `flow office bridge` as a background service that starts at login (launchd LaunchAgent on macOS, Task Scheduler on Windows, systemd user service on Linux). Use the same XDG_CONFIG_HOME, clear FLOW_URL and FLOW_API_KEY overrides, and ensure the service can find Node.js, Git and the Flow CLI. Start it now.
5. Verify that the reporter appears in the 3D office by checking `flow office agents list --json` with the same configuration and telling me which source and how many agents are connected.
```

To set it up manually:

- Install the CLI (Node 22.13 or newer): `npm install -g github:aribradshaw/flow` gives you `flow`. From a checkout of Flow, `npm link` does the same, or run `node tools/flow.mjs …`.
- Create an API key in Flow under **Settings › Connect**: **New key**, any environment (or all), **Read & write**.
- Sign the CLI in: `flow login --url https://your-flow.example --key flow_…` (or `--key-stdin`).
- Try it: `flow office bridge --once --dry-run` prints what would be sent. `flow office bridge --once` sends one report and prints the answer.
- Run it: `flow office bridge` (`flow office bridge --help` lists its options).

To keep it running in the background:

- **Linux** (systemd user service). Save as `~/.config/systemd/user/flow-office-bridge.service`, then `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now flow-office-bridge` (and `loginctl enable-linger $USER` to keep it running when you are logged out):

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Flow office bridge
After=network-online.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/env flow office bridge
Restart=always
RestartSec=10

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

- **macOS** (launchd). Save as `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.flow-office-bridge.plist` with `ProgramArguments` set to the full path of `flow` (see `which flow`), `office`, `bridge`, and `RunAtLoad` and `KeepAlive` true, then `launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.flow-office-bridge.plist`.
- **Windows.** Run it in the background with `start /b flow office bridge` from a terminal, or at every sign-in with a scheduled task: `schtasks /Create /SC ONLOGON /TN "Flow office bridge" /TR "cmd /c flow office bridge"`.

The bridge stores nothing itself: the server and key come from `flow login` (or `FLOW_URL` and `FLOW_API_KEY`).

### The reporter API

Anything can report agents the same way, such as a home-server dashboard. Authenticate with an API key with the `write` scope; agents belong to the key's owner.

- `PUT /api/v1/office/agents` (`office.agents.report`) with `{source, at, agents:[…]}`. Each agent: `id` (stable within the source), `title`, `vendor` (`claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `deepseek`, `grok` or `other`; with `other` the mascot is picked from the model when it names one), `model`, `status` (`running`, `waiting` or `idle`), `activity`, `activityKind` (optional, see [Activity kinds](#activity-kinds)), `host`, `hostLabel`, `repo` (`{name, remote}` or `null`), `children` (subagents: `id`, `title`, `vendor`, `model`, `status`, `activityKind`), `pending` (`null`, or `{requestId, kind: approval | question, summary, can: ["allow","deny"]}`) `agentflow` (optional, `{agent: "<AgentFlow agent id or name>", card: <card number or id>}`: the AgentFlow agent and card it works on, which seat it at that agent's desk; see [Seats](#seats)) `can` (optional, `["message","stop"]`: what the owner may do from the office besides Allow / Deny; list only what this reporter can carry out, `[]` or none for agents that can only be steered where they run) and `transcript` (optional, `[{role: user | assistant | tool, text, at}]`, oldest first: the last 12 are kept, each `text` up to 400 characters, other roles dropped; shown only to the owner, and masked again on the server) and `usage` (optional, `{tokens, costUsd}` for the reporter’s local day. Each field is independently optional and must be finite and nonnegative. Someone who cannot see the agent does not receive it), `role` (optional, `"conductor"` for the person's [Chief of Staff](#chief-of-staff); a conductor is private to everyone but its owner, whatever its repo: they see only that it is one, and its status) and `reply` (optional, a conductor's latest reply, `{text, at, cards}`: `text` up to 600 characters, `cards` up to 12 card numbers; owner only, like the transcript, and masked again on the server). Each source replaces only its own agents; up to 200 agents and 20 children each are kept, long strings are cut, and credentials in a remote are dropped. The answer is `{actions:[…]}`: the actions for this source not yet delivered (see the next item).
- `GET /api/v1/office/actions?source=…&wait=25` (`office.actions.wait`): a long-poll that answers as soon as an answer is queued, or with an empty list after `wait` seconds (up to 30). Each action is delivered once and has a `kind`: `answer` is Allow / Deny, `{id, agentId, kind: "answer", requestId, decision, at}` (treat a missing `kind` as `answer`: servers before this change sent none); `message` is `{id, agentId, kind: "message", text, at}`, up to 2000 characters to send to the agent as a new user turn; `stop` is `{id, agentId, kind: "stop", at}`, to interrupt its running turn. Messages and stops come only from the agent's owner, only for agents whose `can` lists them, and at most 3 messages in a row per agent (then one every 10 seconds), 2 stops (then one every 30 seconds) and 10 of either per person (then one every 6 seconds). Before carrying one out, check it is still the same agent on your side.
- `POST /api/v1/office/actions/{id}` (`office.actions.result`) with `{ok, message}`: how carrying it out went. The agent's owner sees the message right away, in the panel and as a notice. Keep it short and never echo a message's text; log messages and stops on your side without their text.
- `GET /api/v1/office/agents` (`office.agents.list`): your agents as Flow holds them.

A source that has not reported for 90 seconds is gone, and its agents leave the office. An answer is accepted only from the agent's owner, and only while that agent is waiting on that same `requestId`; carry it out only after checking the request is still open on your side. The same operations are MCP tools (`office_agents_report`, …) and CLI commands (`flow office agents report`).

#### Activity kinds

`activityKind` says what kind of work an agent is doing, for its animation. It is one of:

| `activityKind` | Use it for | In the office |
|---|---|---|
| `edit` | Changing files (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, `apply_patch`) | Types at its keyboard |
| `read` | Reading files or docs (Read, View) | Reads a floating book |
| `search` | Searching the code (Grep, Glob, `rg`, find) | Sweeps a magnifying glass |
| `run` | Shell commands (Bash, shell) that are not tests | Terminal glyphs on its screen |
| `test` | Running tests (`npm test`, `pytest`, `cargo test`, …) | A bubbling test tube, flashing green and red |
| `think` | Thinking, planning, writing its answer | A thought cloud |
| `web` | WebFetch, WebSearch, a browser | A spinning globe |
| `idle` | Nothing | Goes for coffee, looks at the board, chats with another idle agent |

It is optional and backward compatible. When it is missing or not one of these, Flow works it out from `activity`: first a tool name at the start (`Edit lib/auth.mjs` is `edit`, `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`, `Bash` and `WebFetch` likewise, and `Bash: npm test` is `test`), then words in it (`Running tests` is `test`, `Reading the docs` is `read`, `Searching for callers` is `search`). Anything else is `think`. An agent whose `status` is `idle` is always `idle`. A subagent's kind is worked out from its `activity` or else its `title`.

Send `activityKind` when your reporter knows the tool an agent is using: it is more accurate than the guess from text. It is shown to everyone who can see the agent, including people who see it only as **Private project**: the kind of work says nothing about the work itself.

### Decorating your room

Inside your own room a **Decorate** button opens a catalogue of props: three plants, a rug, a lamp, a bookshelf, a sofa, an armchair, a coffee table, a poster, a trophy, an aquarium, an arcade cabinet, a bean bag, a standing desk, a whiteboard, a neon sign and a trinket. The ghost snaps to a 0.25 m grid, and wall pieces (posters, the whiteboard, the neon sign) snap onto a wall. R rotates a floor piece, Delete removes the selected one, and Esc leaves the mode. A room holds at most 40 props. They cannot sit outside the room or block the door, a desk, the board or a path, and solid props become obstacles for you and for agents walking through the room. Rugs and wall pieces do not.

A theme sets the floor and wall from a fixed palette (paint, wood, plaster or tile), or one of four presets: Minimal, Cozy, Neon and Nautical. The neon sign takes a short line of text, up to 20 characters, with control characters and markup stripped.

`POST /api/office/{env}/decorate` with `{theme, props}` saves that room for its owner only. The server checks the same rules as the page and does not trust a room size sent by the client. Everyone in the office hears a `decor` event, and the next snapshot includes `decor` for each member. It is stored with the office's other durable state (Postgres, or the file fallback).

### Sharing

An office's members are its environment's owner and the recipient of every active share of that environment (any scope; a whole-environment share also shows all its projects and AgentFlow agents). Opening an environment shared with you as a whole (docs/sharing.md, `share-<shareId>`) opens the owner environment's office: `/api/office/share-<shareId>/…` resolves to it for the share's recipient and is 404 for anyone else, like any office you are not a member of. What each viewer sees there follows [Who sees what](#who-sees-what), per viewer, unchanged.

The snapshot carries `portals: [{env, label, sub, own}]`, the doors for this viewer (computed on the server from their shares). When a share is made or revoked, open offices get a `portals` event with their doors as they are now, so a door appears or goes at once. Access is checked again on every heartbeat, and at once when a share is revoked (from the app, the API or MCP): a stream that lost access gets a `gone` event and is closed, and its person leaves the office for everyone else.

### How it runs

The office is live over Server-Sent Events: `GET /api/office/{env}/events` sends a snapshot (rooms, AgentFlow agents, live agents as this viewer may see them, who is here, each member's presence, and the last 50 Office chat lines, and the viewer's own live reporter sources), then moves, presence, chat, emotes, agent updates and answer results as they happen, with a heartbeat every 15 seconds. Moves (including an optional short status line saved with last-seen), chat (up to 280 characters), emotes, room decor, answers and steering are small POSTs to `/api/office/{env}/presence`, `say`, `emote`, `decorate`, `answer` and `steer` (`{kind: "message", source, agentId, text}` or `{kind: "stop", source, agentId}`; `answer` takes the same body, and a body without `kind` is Allow / Deny). Presence is `POST /api/office/{env}/status` with `available`, `focus`, `dnd` or `away` and a note of up to 60 characters. A knock, letting someone in, and walking into an open room are `POST /api/office/{env}/knock`, `admit` and `enter`. All of these are rate-limited per person. There is no API key operation for sending messages or stops: they come only from the signed-in owner in the office. Only the app's own page can call them, signed in. Send Nearby or Office chat with `{channel: "nearby" | "office", text}`; legacy `{text}` posts to Office. Direct chat uses `POST /api/chat/send` with `{office: {env, target}, body}`, where `target` is the recipient's office member key. The events stream also takes an API key with the `read` scope for that environment (`Authorization: Bearer flow_…`), so a dashboard can watch the office. A stream that stops hearing heartbeats reconnects by itself; the header says "Reconnecting…" only after eight seconds without a stream.

Voice (`lib/office-rtc.mjs`, `public/office-voice.js`) is signalled through the office stream. Each open connection gets an opaque peer id (`rtc {type: "welcome", peer, peers}`). The browser posts `POST /api/office/{env}/rtc {from, to, type, data}`, where `type` is `state` (its voice state: `room`, `near`, `dnd`, `muted`, `share`; sent to the whole office) or `offer`, `answer`, `ice` or `bye` (sent to the one peer `to`). The server checks that `from` is one of the caller's own open connections and that `to` is in the same office. An `offer` also needs both people in the same room's call, or both with proximity voice on outside rooms and neither in Do not disturb. Payloads are capped at 24 KB and rate-limited per connection. They are passed on as `rtc` events and never stored or logged. `GET /api/office/{env}/rtc` returns `{iceServers, ttl, turn}` for `RTCPeerConnection`.

Alerts outside the office use one more stream, `GET /api/office/alerts`, which the app keeps open only while **Notify me when agents wait** is on. It belongs to the signed-in person and has no environment: it sends `mine` (`{waiting:[…]}`, their own agents that are waiting now) when it opens and whenever that changes, and `waiting` (one agent) each time one of their agents starts waiting or waits on a new prompt. An agent's first report from a source (a reporter starting, or the server restarting) does not count as starting to wait. Only the app's own page can open it, signed in; API keys cannot.

During a reconnect, the office keeps the last scene and chat. The next snapshot updates that scene, and each browser sends its last position and status again. A source event ID identifies the previous connection; the server sends a fresh, access-checked snapshot on each connection. Reports keep their original timestamps, and a report still expires 90 seconds after the server last received it. The latest 50 Office chat lines per office, member status and last-seen times, each person's look, and recent actions are saved in Postgres or under `BACKUP_DIR`. Live avatar positions remain in memory. Office actions are claimed before they are returned, so a restart cannot return an already claimed action a second time. If the connection dies between the claim and the response, the reporter can miss that action.

The 24 hour sparkline of how many agents are running (one sample a minute, per member) stays in memory, and is kept across a restart only when a persistence module exports sparkline load and save.

The office is drawn with [Three.js](https://threejs.org) (MIT), vendored in `public/vendor/three` and loaded only when the office opens.

# Using the API

Every operation is an HTTP call under the base URL of your Flow server:

```sh
curl -sS "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/$FLOW_ENV/cards" -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

Keys look like `flow_…` and carry a scope: `read` (list and get), `write` (create, update and move) or `admin` (keys, sharing and environments). The OpenAPI document is at `/api/v1/openapi.json`. Errors come back with an HTTP status plus a `code` and a `message`. Path parameters such as `{env}` are filled from the input. Any other input is sent as the query string for GET and DELETE, or as the JSON body otherwise.

## Environments

### `envs.list`

List environments

`GET /api/v1/envs` · scope `read` · MCP tool `envs_list`

Environments (workspaces) you own, newest first. Use an id from here as {env} in every other call. What others share with you is inside the environment you added it to: a chart named "Shared · <their environment>" (unless you moved its cards), with ids sh.<share>.<id>. Edits to it go back to its owner when the share allows them.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].visibility` | enum | yes | One of `private`, `public`. |
| `items[].owner` | string |  |  |
| `items[].rev` | integer | yes |  |
| `items[].updatedAt` | string | null |  |  |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |

**Example: Your environments**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "default-workspace",
      "name": "Default workspace",
      "visibility": "private",
      "owner": "owner@example.test",
      "rev": 42,
      "updatedAt": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null
}
```

### `envs.get`

Get an environment

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}` · scope `read` · MCP tool `envs_get`

One environment: name, visibility, owner, revision and how much it holds.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `environment` | object | yes |  |
| `environment.id` | string | yes |  |
| `environment.name` | string | yes |  |
| `environment.visibility` | enum | yes | One of `private`, `public`. |
| `environment.owner` | string |  |  |
| `environment.rev` | integer | yes |  |
| `environment.updatedAt` | string | null |  |  |
| `environment.counts` | object |  |  |

**Example: Default workspace**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "environment": {
    "id": "default-workspace",
    "name": "Default workspace",
    "visibility": "private",
    "owner": "owner@example.test",
    "rev": 42,
    "updatedAt": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "counts": {
      "charts": 1,
      "nodes": 7,
      "edges": 7,
      "projects": 3,
      "items": 12,
      "cards": 40
    }
  }
}
```

## Nodes

### `nodes.list`

List nodes

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/charts/{chart}/nodes` · scope `read` · MCP tool `nodes_list`

Cards on a chart (entities, people, areas, notes). Filter by `type`, or by `q` (name contains).

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `chart` | string | yes | Chart id, or "active" for the chart open in the app. |
| `type` | enum |  | One of `entity`, `person`, `area`, `note`. |
| `q` | string |  |  |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].type` | enum | yes | One of `entity`, `person`, `area`, `note`. |
| `items[].x` | number | yes |  |
| `items[].y` | number | yes |  |
| `items[].w` | number |  |  |
| `items[].h` | number |  |  |
| `items[].notes` | string |  |  |
| `items[].image` | string |  | Person photo: an https URL or a data:image/(png\|jpeg\|webp);base64 URL. |
| `items[].email` | string |  | Person email, matching them to an account. |
| `items[].opidUser` | string |  | Read only: the OneProfileID account the person linked this card to, so it shows their account photo. Only that person can link it, from the app. Changing or removing the card's email unlinks it. |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |

**Example: People on the active chart**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/charts/active/nodes?type=person" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "cleo",
      "name": "Cleo Park",
      "type": "person",
      "x": 320,
      "y": 144,
      "notes": ""
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null,
  "rev": 42
}
```

### `nodes.create`

Create a node

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/charts/{chart}/nodes` · scope `write` · MCP tool `nodes_create`

Add a card to a chart. Without x/y it is placed at the origin, stepping 32px diagonally past occupied spots (as the app does). On a share's chart ("Shared · …") it is added to the share's owner when the share lets you add (pending: true while it waits for their approval); a share that does not is refused with 403 share_adds_off.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `chart` | string | yes | Chart id, or "active" for the chart open in the app. |
| `type` | enum | yes | One of `entity`, `person`, `area`, `note`. |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `notes` | string |  |  |
| `w` | number |  |  |
| `h` | number |  |  |
| `image` | string |  | Person cards only: a photo as an https URL, or a data:image/(png\|jpeg\|webp);base64 URL up to 61440 characters. "" removes it. |
| `email` | string |  | Person cards only: their email, so the app can show the matching account photo. Never shared with share recipients. Changing or removing it unlinks the card from its OneProfileID account. "" removes it. |
| `x` | number |  |  |
| `y` | number |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `node` | object | yes |  |
| `node.id` | string | yes |  |
| `node.name` | string | yes |  |
| `node.type` | enum | yes | One of `entity`, `person`, `area`, `note`. |
| `node.x` | number | yes |  |
| `node.y` | number | yes |  |
| `node.w` | number |  |  |
| `node.h` | number |  |  |
| `node.notes` | string |  |  |
| `node.image` | string |  | Person photo: an https URL or a data:image/(png\|jpeg\|webp);base64 URL. |
| `node.email` | string |  | Person email, matching them to an account. |
| `node.opidUser` | string |  | Read only: the OneProfileID account the person linked this card to, so it shows their account photo. Only that person can link it, from the app. Changing or removing the card's email unlinks it. |
| `pending` | boolean |  | Only when true: the record was added inside a share whose owner approves additions, and waits for them (docs/sharing.md). It shows as "Pending approval" until they approve or deny it. |

**Example: Add a person**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/charts/active/nodes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"type":"person","name":"Cleo Park","x":320,"y":144}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 43,
  "node": {
    "id": "cleo",
    "name": "Cleo Park",
    "type": "person",
    "x": 320,
    "y": 144,
    "notes": ""
  }
}
```

### `edges.create`

Create an edge

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/charts/{chart}/edges` · scope `write` · MCP tool `edges_create`

Connect two cards on the same chart. A second edge between the same pair (same direction) is refused with 409. Joining two cards of the same share adds the connection to its owner, as nodes.create does.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `chart` | string | yes | Chart id, or "active" for the chart open in the app. |
| `from` | string | yes | Node id. |
| `to` | string | yes | Node id. |
| `type` | enum |  | One of `ownership`, `group`. |
| `percent` | string | number |  | 0-100, or "" for unspecified. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `edge` | object | yes |  |
| `edge.id` | string | yes |  |
| `edge.from` | string | yes |  |
| `edge.to` | string | yes |  |
| `edge.type` | enum | yes | One of `ownership`, `group`. |
| `edge.percent` | string | yes |  |
| `pending` | boolean |  | Only when true: the record was added inside a share whose owner approves additions, and waits for them (docs/sharing.md). It shows as "Pending approval" until they approve or deny it. |

**Example: 50% ownership**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/charts/active/edges" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"from":"cleo","to":"quill","percent":"50"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 45,
  "edge": {
    "id": "o1",
    "from": "cleo",
    "to": "quill",
    "type": "ownership",
    "percent": "50"
  }
}
```

### `edges.update`

Update an edge

`PATCH /api/v1/envs/{env}/charts/{chart}/edges/{edge}` · scope `write` · MCP tool `edges_update`

Change a connection's ownership percent or its type, keeping the edge. Fields left out stay as they are; a group edge carries no percent. On a share's chart an edit share lets you change the percent, and the change goes back to its owner; the type stays the owner's.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `chart` | string | yes | Chart id, or "active" for the chart open in the app. |
| `edge` | string | yes | Edge id. |
| `type` | enum |  | One of `ownership`, `group`. |
| `percent` | string | number |  | 0-100, or "" for unspecified. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `edge` | object | yes |  |
| `edge.id` | string | yes |  |
| `edge.from` | string | yes |  |
| `edge.to` | string | yes |  |
| `edge.type` | enum | yes | One of `ownership`, `group`. |
| `edge.percent` | string | yes |  |

**Example: Full ownership**

```sh
curl -sS -X PATCH "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/charts/active/edges/o1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"percent":"100"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 46,
  "edge": {
    "id": "o1",
    "from": "cleo",
    "to": "quill",
    "type": "ownership",
    "percent": "100"
  }
}
```

### `edges.delete`

Delete an edge

`DELETE /api/v1/envs/{env}/charts/{chart}/edges/{edge}` · scope `write` · MCP tool `edges_delete`

Remove one connection. The cards it joined stay. Earlier revisions are kept in the workspace history.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `chart` | string | yes | Chart id, or "active" for the chart open in the app. |
| `edge` | string | yes | Edge id. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `deleted` | string | yes |  |

**Example: Delete**

```json
  "deleted": "o1"
}
```

## Projects

### `projects.list`

Timeline/board projects (coloured tags), optionally only those under one chart entity or area.

**Input**

| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |

| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |

```json
    {

      "name": "Lantern",
      "color": "#7cb980",
      "entity": "flygon"
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null,
  "rev": 42
}
```

### `projects.create`

Create a project

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/projects` · scope `write` · MCP tool `projects_create`

Add a project. Names are unique (case-insensitive); a duplicate gets 409. Without a colour the next palette colour is used. Under a shared entity, or with share, it is added to that share's owner when the share lets you add (pending: true while it waits for their approval).

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `color` | string |  | Hex colour, e.g. #7cb980. |
| `entity` | string |  | The chart entity or area it sits under: node id or name; "" for none. |
| `repos` | string[] |  | Code repositories that belong to the project: a name ("flow"), owner/name ("acme/flow") or a git remote URL. The 3D office shows a teammate's live agent working in one of them to everyone who can see this project. Replaces the list; [] clears it. |
| `share` | string |  | Add it to the owner of a share placed in this environment (the <share> in its sh.<share>.<id> ids), when that share lets you add. Without it, a record that refers to a share's records (a card in a shared project, say) goes to that share's owner anyway. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `project` | object | yes |  |
| `project.id` | string | yes |  |
| `project.name` | string | yes |  |
| `project.color` | string | yes |  |
| `project.entity` | string | yes |  |
| `project.repos` | string[] |  | Code repositories that belong to the project (absent when none). |
| `pending` | boolean |  | Only when true: the record was added inside a share whose owner approves additions, and waits for them (docs/sharing.md). It shows as "Pending approval" until they approve or deny it. |

**Example: Under Kestrel Group**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/projects" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Lantern","color":"#7cb980","entity":"Kestrel Group"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 47,
  "project": {
    "id": "p1",
    "name": "Lantern",
    "color": "#7cb980",
    "entity": "flygon"
  }
}
```

| `repos` | string[] |  | Code repositories that belong to the project: a name ("flow"), owner/name ("acme/flow") or a git remote URL. The 3D office shows a teammate's live agent working in one of them to everyone who can see this project. Replaces the list; [] clears it. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

## Timeline

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/items` · scope `read` · MCP tool `items_list`

Timeline items (milestones, releases, features...). Filter by project (id or name), kind, status or `q` (title contains). Items with start "" are backlog.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `project` | string |  | Project id or name. |

| `status` | enum |  | One of `planned`, `active`, `risk`, `blocked`, `done`, `cancelled`. |
| `q` | string |  |  |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].kind` | enum | yes | One of `feature`, `milestone`, `release`, `deadline`, `project`, `phase`, `event`. |
| `items[].status` | enum | yes | One of `planned`, `active`, `risk`, `blocked`, `done`, `cancelled`. |

### `items.create`

Create a timeline item

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/items` · scope `write` · MCP tool `items_create`

Add a timeline item. Without a start date it is backlog (Board and List only). Kind defaults to milestone when dated, feature otherwise. Tagged only with shared projects, or with share, it is added to that share's owner when the share lets you add (pending: true while it waits for their approval).

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `kind` | enum |  | One of `feature`, `milestone`, `release`, `deadline`, `project`, `phase`, `event`. |
| `status` | enum |  | One of `planned`, `active`, `risk`, `blocked`, `done`, `cancelled`. |
| `start` | string |  | YYYY-MM-DD, or "" for none. |
| `end` | string |  | YYYY-MM-DD, or "" for none. |
| `priority` | enum |  | One of `high`, `medium`, `low`, ``. |
| `release` | string |  | A release item: id or title; "" for none. |
| `projects` | string[] |  |  |
| `owner` | string |  |  |
| `link` | string |  |  |
| `notes` | string |  |  |
| `share` | string |  | Add it to the owner of a share placed in this environment (the <share> in its sh.<share>.<id> ids), when that share lets you add. Without it, a record that refers to a share's records (a card in a shared project, say) goes to that share's owner anyway. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `item` | object | yes |  |
| `item.id` | string | yes |  |
| `item.title` | string | yes |  |
| `item.kind` | enum | yes | One of `feature`, `milestone`, `release`, `deadline`, `project`, `phase`, `event`. |
| `item.status` | enum | yes | One of `planned`, `active`, `risk`, `blocked`, `done`, `cancelled`. |
| `item.start` | string | yes |  |
| `item.end` | string | yes |  |
| `item.priority` | string |  |  |
| `item.release` | string |  |  |
| `item.projects` | string[] | yes |  |
| `item.owner` | string |  |  |
| `item.link` | string |  |  |
| `item.notes` | string |  |  |
| `pending` | boolean |  | Only when true: the record was added inside a share whose owner approves additions, and waits for them (docs/sharing.md). It shows as "Pending approval" until they approve or deny it. |

**Example: A release**

## DevOps cards

### `cards.list`

List DevOps cards

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/cards` · scope `read` · MCP tool `cards_list`

Board cards in board order. Filters: column, project (id, name or "none"), label (id or name), assignee (person id or name), agent (AgentFlow agent: cards delegated to it), q ("#12" or title text), hideDone, snoozed (true: only cards snoozed now; false: only awake ones; left out: both).

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `column` | string |  | Board column: requests (Requests / Sprinted), doing (Doing), blocked (Blocked), uat (UAT), done (Done), must (Backlog: Must Have), nice (Backlog: Nice to Have). One of `requests`, `doing`, `blocked`, `uat`, `done`, `must`, `nice`. |
| `project` | string |  | Project id or name, or "none". |
| `label` | string |  | Label id or name. |
| `assignee` | string |  | Person node id or name, or a share member (@email or email). |
| `agent` | string |  | AgentFlow agent id or name: cards delegated to it. |
| `q` | string |  |  |
| `hideDone` | boolean |  |  |
| `snoozed` | boolean |  | true: only cards snoozed now; false: leave them out. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].number` | integer | yes |  |
| `items[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].description` | string |  |  |
| `items[].column` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].project` | string |  |  |
| `items[].labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `items[].points` | number | null |  |  |
| `items[].actual` | number | null |  | Points the card actually took, recorded after the work (for example from the agents' token use). Separate from points, the up-front estimate. |
| `items[].due` | string |  |  |
| `items[].snoozedUntil` | string | null |  | When the snooze ends (ISO time). Until then the board hides the card for everyone (a column header can show its snoozed cards); afterwards it is a normal card again. null when not snoozed. |
| `items[].assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].item` | string |  |  |
| `items[].created` | string |  |  |
| `items[].updated` | string |  |  |
| `items[].moved` | string |  |  |
| `items[].agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |

**Example: Open cards for a project**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards?project=Lantern&hideDone=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "k1",
      "number": 12,
      "title": "Build sign-up form",
      "description": "",
      "column": "requests",
      "project": "p1",
      "labels": [
        "l-high"
      ],
      "points": 3,
      "actual": null,
      "due": "2026-11-15",
      "assignees": [
        {
          "node": "cleo",
          "role": "developer"
        }
      ],
      "checklist": [
        {
          "id": "x1",
          "text": "Email field",
          "done": false
        }
      ],
      "links": [],
      "item": "i1",
      "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
      "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
      "moved": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
      "snoozedUntil": null,
      "agents": [
        "a1"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null,
  "rev": 42
}
```

### `cards.get`

Get a DevOps card

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/cards/{card}` · scope `read` · MCP tool `cards_get`

One card by number ("12" or "#12") or id.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `card` | string | integer | yes | Card number or id. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `card` | object | yes |  |
| `card.id` | string | yes |  |
| `card.number` | integer | yes |  |
| `card.title` | string | yes |  |
| `card.description` | string |  |  |
| `card.column` | string | yes |  |
| `card.project` | string |  |  |
| `card.labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `card.points` | number | null |  |  |
| `card.actual` | number | null |  | Points the card actually took, recorded after the work (for example from the agents' token use). Separate from points, the up-front estimate. |
| `card.due` | string |  |  |
| `card.snoozedUntil` | string | null |  | When the snooze ends (ISO time). Until then the board hides the card for everyone (a column header can show its snoozed cards); afterwards it is a normal card again. null when not snoozed. |
| `card.assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.item` | string |  |  |
| `card.created` | string |  |  |
| `card.updated` | string |  |  |
| `card.moved` | string |  |  |
| `card.agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |

**Example: Card #12**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards/12" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "rev": 42,
  "card": {
    "id": "k1",
    "number": 12,
    "title": "Build sign-up form",
    "description": "",
    "column": "requests",
    "project": "p1",
    "labels": [
      "l-high"
    ],
    "points": 3,
    "actual": null,
    "due": "2026-11-15",
    "assignees": [
      {
        "node": "cleo",
        "role": "developer"
      }
    ],
    "checklist": [
      {
        "id": "x1",
        "text": "Email field",
        "done": false
      }
    ],
    "links": [],
    "item": "i1",
    "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "moved": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "snoozedUntil": null,
    "agents": [
      "a1"
    ]
  }
}
```

### `cards.create`

Create a DevOps card

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/cards` · scope `write` · MCP tool `cards_create`

Add a card (it gets the next #number). Lands in Requests / Sprinted unless `column` says otherwise. References (project, labels, assignees, item) are ids or names; unknown ones are refused with 400. In a shared project, or with share, it is added to that share's owner when the share lets you add (pending: true while it waits for their approval; the owner numbers it); a share that does not is refused with 403 share_adds_off.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `column` | string |  | Board column: requests (Requests / Sprinted), doing (Doing), blocked (Blocked), uat (UAT), done (Done), must (Backlog: Must Have), nice (Backlog: Nice to Have). One of `requests`, `doing`, `blocked`, `uat`, `done`, `must`, `nice`. |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `project` | string |  | Project id or name; "" for none. |
| `labels` | string[] |  |  |
| `points` | number | null |  |  |
| `actual` | number | null |  | Points the card actually took, recorded after the work (for example from the agents' token use). Separate from points, the up-front estimate. |
| `due` | string |  | YYYY-MM-DD, or "" for none. |
| `snoozedUntil` | string | null |  | Snooze the card until this time: an ISO time such as 2026-11-23T16:00:00Z (include Z or a time zone offset). "" or null wakes it. A time already past wakes it too. |
| `assignees` | object[] |  |  |
| `assignees[].node` | string | yes | A person on a chart (node id or name), or someone the card is shared with (@email, email or name). |
| `assignees[].role` | enum |  | One of `developer`, `tester`, `requester`. |
| `checklist` | object[] |  |  |
| `checklist[].id` | string |  |  |
| `checklist[].text` | string | yes |  |
| `checklist[].done` | boolean |  |  |
| `links` | object[] |  |  |
| `links[].id` | string |  |  |
| `links[].kind` | enum |  | One of `pr`, `commit`, `url`. |
| `links[].url` | string | yes |  |
| `item` | string |  | Timeline item id or title; "" for none. |
| `agents` | string[] |  | Delegate the card to these agents (replaces the list; [] for none). It joins each one's work queue (agents.work). |
| `share` | string |  | Add it to the owner of a share placed in this environment (the <share> in its sh.<share>.<id> ids), when that share lets you add. Without it, a record that refers to a share's records (a card in a shared project, say) goes to that share's owner anyway. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `card` | object | yes |  |
| `card.id` | string | yes |  |
| `card.number` | integer | yes |  |
| `card.title` | string | yes |  |
| `card.description` | string |  |  |
| `card.column` | string | yes |  |
| `card.project` | string |  |  |
| `card.labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `card.points` | number | null |  |  |
| `card.actual` | number | null |  | Points the card actually took, recorded after the work (for example from the agents' token use). Separate from points, the up-front estimate. |
| `card.due` | string |  |  |
| `card.snoozedUntil` | string | null |  | When the snooze ends (ISO time). Until then the board hides the card for everyone (a column header can show its snoozed cards); afterwards it is a normal card again. null when not snoozed. |
| `card.assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.item` | string |  |  |
| `card.created` | string |  |  |
| `card.updated` | string |  |  |
| `card.moved` | string |  |  |
| `card.agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |
| `pending` | boolean |  | Only when true: the record was added inside a share whose owner approves additions, and waits for them (docs/sharing.md). It shows as "Pending approval" until they approve or deny it. |

**Example: New card**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Build sign-up form","project":"Lantern","labels":["High"],"points":3,"due":"2026-11-15","assignees":[{"node":"Cleo Park","role":"developer"}],"checklist":[{"text":"Email field"}],"item":"Public beta"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 51,
  "card": {
    "id": "k1",
    "number": 12,
    "title": "Build sign-up form",
    "description": "",
    "column": "requests",
    "project": "p1",
    "labels": [
      "l-high"
    ],
    "points": 3,
    "actual": null,
    "due": "2026-11-15",
    "assignees": [
      {
        "node": "cleo",
        "role": "developer"
      }
    ],
    "checklist": [
      {
        "id": "x1",
        "text": "Email field",
        "done": false
      }
    ],
    "links": [],
    "item": "i1",
    "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "moved": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "snoozedUntil": null,
    "agents": [
      "a1"
    ]
  }
}
```

### `cards.update`

Update a DevOps card

`PATCH /api/v1/envs/{env}/cards/{card}` · scope `write` · MCP tool `cards_update`

Change a card's fields. Lists you send (labels, assignees, checklist, links) replace the old ones. snoozedUntil snoozes the card until an ISO time ("" or null wakes it). The column only changes through cards.move, which applies the board's gates. A description you send replaces the old one: to add to it, read the card and send ifUpdated (its `updated`), so a change someone made meanwhile is refused with 409 card_changed instead of lost.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `card` | string | integer | yes | Card number or id. |
| `title` | string |  |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `project` | string |  | Project id or name; "" for none. |
| `labels` | string[] |  |  |
| `points` | number | null |  |  |
| `actual` | number | null |  | Points the card actually took, recorded after the work (for example from the agents' token use). Separate from points, the up-front estimate. |
| `due` | string |  | YYYY-MM-DD, or "" for none. |
| `snoozedUntil` | string | null |  | Snooze the card until this time: an ISO time such as 2026-11-23T16:00:00Z (include Z or a time zone offset). "" or null wakes it. A time already past wakes it too. |
| `assignees` | object[] |  |  |
| `assignees[].node` | string | yes | A person on a chart (node id or name), or someone the card is shared with (@email, email or name). |
| `assignees[].role` | enum |  | One of `developer`, `tester`, `requester`. |
| `checklist` | object[] |  |  |
| `checklist[].id` | string |  |  |
| `checklist[].text` | string | yes |  |
| `checklist[].done` | boolean |  |  |
| `links` | object[] |  |  |
| `links[].id` | string |  |  |
| `links[].kind` | enum |  | One of `pr`, `commit`, `url`. |
| `links[].url` | string | yes |  |
| `item` | string |  | Timeline item id or title; "" for none. |
| `agents` | string[] |  | Delegate the card to these agents (replaces the list; [] for none). It joins each one's work queue (agents.work). |
| `ifUpdated` | string |  | The card's `updated` as you read it (cards.get). If the card changed since, nothing is written: 409 card_changed, with the current card in details.card. Read it again and reapply your change. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `card` | object | yes |  |
| `card.id` | string | yes |  |
| `card.number` | integer | yes |  |
| `card.title` | string | yes |  |
| `card.description` | string |  |  |
| `card.column` | string | yes |  |
| `card.project` | string |  |  |
| `card.labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `card.points` | number | null |  |  |
| `card.actual` | number | null |  | Points the card actually took, recorded after the work (for example from the agents' token use). Separate from points, the up-front estimate. |
| `card.due` | string |  |  |
| `card.snoozedUntil` | string | null |  | When the snooze ends (ISO time). Until then the board hides the card for everyone (a column header can show its snoozed cards); afterwards it is a normal card again. null when not snoozed. |
| `card.assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.item` | string |  |  |
| `card.created` | string |  |  |
| `card.updated` | string |  |  |
| `card.moved` | string |  |  |
| `card.agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |

**Example: Tick the checklist**

```sh
curl -sS -X PATCH "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards/12" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"checklist":[{"id":"x1","text":"Email field","done":true}]}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 52,
  "card": {
    "id": "k1",
    "number": 12,
    "title": "Build sign-up form",
    "description": "",
    "column": "requests",
    "project": "p1",
    "labels": [
      "l-high"
    ],
    "points": 3,
    "actual": null,
    "due": "2026-11-15",
    "assignees": [
      {
        "node": "cleo",
        "role": "developer"
      }
    ],
    "checklist": [
      {
        "id": "x1",
        "text": "Email field",
        "done": true
      }
    ],
    "links": [],
    "item": "i1",
    "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "moved": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "snoozedUntil": null,
    "agents": [
      "a1"
    ]
  }
}
```

```sh
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
```

### `cards.move`

Move a DevOps card

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/cards/{card}/move` · scope `write` · MCP tool `cards_move`

Move a card to a column (and position: `index` among that column's other cards; end if left out). The board's gates apply: into Done needs `confirm: true`, or `approve: true` from UAT (the Approve button); out of Done needs `confirm: true`; into Doing without a developer needs `developer` (a person, who is assigned) or `confirm: true` to leave it unassigned. A refused gate is 409 with code confirm_done, confirm_reopen or pick_developer. ifUpdated (the card's `updated` as you read it) refuses the move with 409 card_changed if the card changed since.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `card` | string | integer | yes | Card number or id. |
| `column` | string | yes | Board column: requests (Requests / Sprinted), doing (Doing), blocked (Blocked), uat (UAT), done (Done), must (Backlog: Must Have), nice (Backlog: Nice to Have). One of `requests`, `doing`, `blocked`, `uat`, `done`, `must`, `nice`. |
| `index` | integer |  |  |
| `confirm` | boolean |  |  |
| `approve` | boolean |  |  |
| `developer` | string |  | Person node id or name, or someone the card is shared with (@email or email). |
| `ifUpdated` | string |  | The card's `updated` as you read it (cards.get). If the card changed since, nothing is written: 409 card_changed, with the current card in details.card. Read it again and reapply your change. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `card` | object | yes |  |
| `card.id` | string | yes |  |
| `card.number` | integer | yes |  |
| `card.title` | string | yes |  |
| `card.description` | string |  |  |
| `card.column` | string | yes |  |
| `card.project` | string |  |  |
| `card.labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `card.points` | number | null |  |  |
| `card.actual` | number | null |  | Points the card actually took, recorded after the work (for example from the agents' token use). Separate from points, the up-front estimate. |
| `card.due` | string |  |  |
| `card.snoozedUntil` | string | null |  | When the snooze ends (ISO time). Until then the board hides the card for everyone (a column header can show its snoozed cards); afterwards it is a normal card again. null when not snoozed. |
| `card.assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.item` | string |  |  |
| `card.created` | string |  |  |
| `card.updated` | string |  |  |
| `card.moved` | string |  |  |
| `card.agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |

**Example: Approve from UAT**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards/12/move" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"column":"done","approve":true}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 53,
  "card": {
    "id": "k1",
    "number": 12,
    "title": "Build sign-up form",
    "description": "",
    "column": "done",
    "project": "p1",
    "labels": [
      "l-high"
    ],
    "points": 3,
    "actual": null,
    "due": "2026-11-15",
    "assignees": [
      {
        "node": "cleo",
        "role": "developer"
      }
    ],
    "checklist": [
      {
        "id": "x1",
        "text": "Email field",
        "done": false
      }
    ],
    "links": [],
    "item": "i1",
    "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "moved": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "snoozedUntil": null,
    "agents": [
      "a1"
    ]
  }
}
```

**Example: Start work**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/cards/12/move" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"column":"doing","developer":"Cleo Park"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 54,
  "card": {
    "id": "k1",
    "number": 12,

      "l-high"
    ],

      }

    "snoozedUntil": null,
    "agents": [
      "a1"
    ]
  }
}
```

### `cards.deleted`

List recently deleted cards

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/deleted-cards` · scope `read` · MCP tool `cards_deleted`

Cards removed from the board in the last 180 days, newest first, whatever removed them: deleting on the board, undo, a snapshot restore or other whole-workspace save, or the API and MCP. Each entry holds the whole card as it was, who removed it (deletedBy, via and, for an API key or MCP client, actor: the key's name), when, and the last revision it was in (fromRev). They outlive the revision history. Bring one back with cards.restore. Filters: q ("#12" or title text); pending: true leaves out the ones already restored.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `q` | string |  |  |
| `pending` | boolean |  |  |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes | Entry id, for cards.restore. |
| `items[].env` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].cardId` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].number` | integer | null | yes |  |
| `items[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].card` | object | yes | The card as it was when it was removed. |
| `items[].deletedAt` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].deletedBy` | string | yes | Email of the account that saved the change. |
| `items[].via` | enum | yes | board (deleted on the board), undo (undo or redo), snapshot (a snapshot restore or other whole-workspace save from a browser), save (a save from an older browser tab), api, mcp, relay. One of `board`, `undo`, `snapshot`, `save`, `api`, `mcp`, `relay`. |
| `items[].actor` | string | yes | The API key's name, when an API key or MCP client removed it. |
| `items[].fromRev` | integer | yes | The last revision the card was in. |
| `items[].rev` | integer | yes | The revision that removed it. |
| `items[].restoredAt` | string | null | yes |  |
| `items[].restoredBy` | string |  |  |
| `items[].restoredNumber` | integer | null |  | The number it was restored as. |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |

**Example: Recently deleted**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/deleted-cards" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "del_6f1c2a4e-0b7d-4c55-9a3e-2d8f1b0c9e11",

      "cardId": "k1",
      "number": 12,
      "title": "Build sign-up form",
      "card": {
        "id": "k1",
        "number": 12,
        "title": "Build sign-up form",
        "description": "",
        "column": "requests",
        "project": "p1",
        "labels": [
          "l-high"
        ],
        "points": 3,

          }

          }
        ],

          "a1"
```

### `cards.restore`

Restore a deleted card

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/deleted-cards/{entry}/restore` · scope `write` · MCP tool `cards_restore`

Put a deleted card back on the board: same id, column, fields, checklist and links, and its agent links where the agents still exist (labels, projects or people since removed are dropped). It keeps its number if no other card has taken it; otherwise it gets the next number, renumbered is true and message says so. entry is an id from cards.deleted, or a card number ("#12") or card id for its latest deletion. A card that is already back is refused with 409 already_restored.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `entry` | string | yes | Entry id from cards.deleted, or a card number ("#12") or card id. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `card` | object | yes |  |
| `card.id` | string | yes |  |
| `card.number` | integer | yes |  |
| `card.title` | string | yes |  |
| `card.description` | string |  |  |
| `card.column` | string | yes |  |
| `card.project` | string |  |  |
| `card.labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `card.points` | number | null |  |  |
| `card.actual` | number | null |  | Points the card actually took, recorded after the work (for example from the agents' token use). Separate from points, the up-front estimate. |
| `card.due` | string |  |  |
| `card.snoozedUntil` | string | null |  | When the snooze ends (ISO time). Until then the board hides the card for everyone (a column header can show its snoozed cards); afterwards it is a normal card again. null when not snoozed. |
| `card.assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `card.item` | string |  |  |
| `card.created` | string |  |  |
| `card.updated` | string |  |  |
| `card.moved` | string |  |  |
| `card.agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |
| `renumbered` | boolean | yes |  |
| `previousNumber` | integer | null | yes | The number it had before, when renumbered. |
| `message` | string | yes |  |

**Example: Restore #12**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/deleted-cards/%2312/restore" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY"
```

```json

  "card": {
    "id": "k1",
    "number": 12,
    "title": "Build sign-up form",
    "description": "",

    "project": "p1",
    "labels": [
      "l-high"
    ],
    "points": 3,
    "actual": null,
    "due": "2026-11-15",
    "assignees": [
      {
        "node": "cleo",
        "role": "developer"
      }
    ],
    "checklist": [
      {
        "id": "x1",
        "text": "Email field",
        "done": false
      }
    ],
    "links": [],
    "item": "i1",
    "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "moved": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "snoozedUntil": null,
    "agents": [
      "a1"
    ]
  },
  "renumbered": false,
  "previousNumber": null,
```

```json
}
```

## Labels

### `labels.list`

List DevOps labels

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/labels` · scope `read` · MCP tool `labels_list`

Board labels with their section (priority, urgency, area, topic, other) and colour token.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `section` | enum |  | One of `priority`, `urgency`, `area`, `topic`, `other`. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

| `items[].color` | string | yes |  |

| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |

### `labels.create`

Create a DevOps label

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/labels` · scope `write` · MCP tool `labels_create`

Add a label. `id` defaults to "l-" plus the name in lower case; a taken id or name gets 409. Colours: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, sky, purple, pink, lime, black, teal, indigo, rose, amber, brown, slate, red-deep.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `id` | string |  |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `section` | enum |  | One of `priority`, `urgency`, `area`, `topic`, `other`. |
| `color` | enum |  | One of `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue`, `sky`, `purple`, `pink`, `lime`, `black`, `teal`, `indigo`, `rose`, `amber`, `brown`, `slate`, `red-deep`. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `label` | object | yes |  |
| `label.id` | string | yes |  |
| `label.name` | string | yes |  |
| `label.section` | enum | yes | One of `priority`, `urgency`, `area`, `topic`, `other`. |
| `label.color` | string | yes |  |

**Example: Research**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/labels" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"l-research","name":"Research","section":"area","color":"teal"}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 55,
  "label": {
    "id": "l-research",
    "name": "Research",
    "section": "area",
    "color": "teal"
  }
}
```

### `agents.work`

Get an agent's work queue

`GET /api/v1/envs/{env}/agents/{agent}/work` · scope `read` · MCP tool `agents_work`

What a runner needs to work as this agent: its `brief` and its queue, the open DevOps cards delegated to it (cards.update agents, or the card's Delegated to picker). A card last changed by someone outside the environment (through an edit share) is left out until the owner changes it again. A snoozed card (snoozedUntil in the future) is left out too, still delegated, and comes back on its own when the snooze ends; includeSnoozed: true keeps snoozed cards in. Order: doing, requests, blocked, uat, must, nice (work in progress first; Blocked and UAT wait on others), then soonest due date, then #number. `columns` narrows the queue, e.g. ["doing","requests"] for cards it can act on now. Report back with cards.update (checklist, links) and cards.move.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `agent` | string | yes | Agent id or name. |
| `columns` | string[] |  | Only these columns (comma-separated in a query string). |
| `includeSnoozed` | boolean |  | true: keep cards that are snoozed now (left out by default). |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1-200, default 50). |
| `cursor` | string |  | nextCursor from the previous page. |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `agent` | object | yes |  |
| `agent.id` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.name` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.kind` | enum | yes | One of `agent`, `human`, `team`, `automation`. |
| `agent.title` | string |  |  |
| `agent.status` | enum | yes | One of `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `retired`. |
| `agent.live` | boolean | yes |  |
| `agent.reportsTo` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.supervisor` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.purpose` | string |  |  |
| `agent.instructions` | string |  |  |
| `agent.runtime` | string |  |  |
| `agent.models` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.model` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.auto` | boolean | yes |  |
| `agent.schedule` | string |  | When it runs: plain text or cron; "" for none. |
| `agent.job` | object |  |  |
| `agent.inputs` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.outputs` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.tools` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.projects` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.cards` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.items` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.created` | string |  |  |
| `agent.updated` | string |  |  |
| `agent.x` | number |  |  |
| `agent.y` | number |  |  |
| `brief` | string | yes |  |
| `items` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].number` | integer | yes |  |
| `items[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].description` | string |  |  |
| `items[].column` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].project` | string |  |  |
| `items[].labels` | string[] | yes |  |
| `items[].points` | number | null |  |  |
| `items[].actual` | number | null |  | Points the card actually took, recorded after the work (for example from the agents' token use). Separate from points, the up-front estimate. |
| `items[].due` | string |  |  |
| `items[].snoozedUntil` | string | null |  | When the snooze ends (ISO time). Until then the board hides the card for everyone (a column header can show its snoozed cards); afterwards it is a normal card again. null when not snoozed. |
| `items[].assignees` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].checklist` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].links` | object[] | yes |  |
| `items[].item` | string |  |  |
| `items[].created` | string |  |  |
| `items[].updated` | string |  |  |
| `items[].moved` | string |  |  |
| `items[].agents` | string[] |  | AgentFlow agents the card is delegated to (ids). |
| `nextCursor` | string | null | yes |  |

**Example: What should the researcher do now?**

```sh
curl -sS -X GET "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/agents/Researcher/work?columns=doing%2Crequests" \
```

### `agents.create`

Create an AgentFlow agent

`POST /api/v1/envs/{env}/agents` · scope `write` · MCP tool `agents_create`

Add an agent to the AgentFlow org chart. References (reportsTo, supervisor, projects, cards, items) are ids or names; unknown ones are refused with 400, and a reporting loop with reports_loop.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `kind` | enum |  | agent (AI agent), human, team, or automation (a scripted job without AI that runs on its own schedule outside Flow: no models, never live). One of `agent`, `human`, `team`, `automation`. |
| `title` | string |  | Role, e.g. Research. |
| `status` | enum |  | One of `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `retired`. |
| `live` | boolean |  | The switch runners obey: false (the default) and runners leave the agent alone; true and the runner named in runtime works its queue. |
| `reportsTo` | string |  | The agent it reports to: id or name; "" for top level. |
| `supervisor` | string |  | A person on a chart who oversees it: node id or name; "" for none. |
| `purpose` | string |  |  |
| `instructions` | string |  | System prompt or runbook. |
| `runtime` | string |  | Where it runs: a runner name from runners.list, e.g. a home server. |
| `models` | string[] |  | Model ids the runner reported (runners.list), in order: the primary first, then fallbacks it tries when one fails (or, with auto, the pool it picks from). Also sets model to the first. Wins over model when both are sent. |
| `model` | string |  | One model id, e.g. claudeAgent:claude-sonnet-5-5: the same as sending models with just it ("" for none). Always reads back as the first of models. |
| `auto` | boolean |  | false (the default): the runner starts on the first of models and falls back in order. true: models is a pool and the runner picks one per card. |
| `schedule` | string |  | When it runs, in plain words or cron, e.g. "Weekdays 09:00" (a note carried in the brief for an AI agent; the reference runner does not start work from it); "" for none. |
| `job` | union |  | The runner job it was promoted from: {runner, id} (see runners.report jobs); null or "" for none. |
| `inputs` | string[] |  | What it takes in. |
| `outputs` | string[] |  | What it produces. |
| `tools` | string[] |  | What it may use. |
| `projects` | string[] |  |  |
| `cards` | string | integer[] |  |  |
| `items` | string[] |  |  |
| `x` | number |  | Canvas position (with y). Leave out to place it under its manager. |
| `y` | number |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | integer | yes | Workspace revision after (or at) this call. |
| `agent` | object | yes |  |
| `agent.id` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.name` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.kind` | enum | yes | One of `agent`, `human`, `team`, `automation`. |
| `agent.title` | string |  |  |
| `agent.status` | enum | yes | One of `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `retired`. |
| `agent.live` | boolean | yes |  |
| `agent.reportsTo` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.supervisor` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.purpose` | string |  |  |
| `agent.instructions` | string |  |  |
| `agent.runtime` | string |  |  |
| `agent.models` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.model` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.auto` | boolean | yes |  |
| `agent.schedule` | string |  | When it runs: plain text or cron; "" for none. |
| `agent.job` | object |  |  |
| `agent.inputs` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.outputs` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.tools` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.projects` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.cards` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.items` | string[] | yes |  |
| `agent.created` | string |  |  |
| `agent.updated` | string |  |  |
| `agent.x` | number |  |  |
| `agent.y` | number |  |  |

**Example: New research agent**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$FLOW_URL/api/v1/envs/default-workspace/agents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Researcher","title":"Research","status":"active","reportsTo":"Chief of staff","supervisor":"Cleo Park","inputs":["A card that needs research"],"outputs":["Research notes on the card"],"cards":["#12"]}'
```

```json
{
  "rev": 56,
  "agent": {
    "id": "a1",
    "name": "Researcher",
    "kind": "agent",
    "title": "Research",
    "status": "active",
    "live": false,
    "reportsTo": "a0",
    "supervisor": "cleo",
    "purpose": "Gathers context before work starts.",
    "instructions": "",
    "runtime": "T3",
    "models": [],
    "model": "",
    "auto": false,
    "schedule": "Weekdays 09:00",
    "inputs": [
      "A card that needs research"
    ],
    "outputs": [
      "Research notes on the card"
    ],
    "tools": [
      "Web search"
    ],
    "projects": [
      "p1"
    ],
    "cards": [
      "k1"
    ],
    "items": [
      "i1"
    ],
    "created": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-29T17:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

### `agents.update`

Update an AgentFlow agent

`PATCH /api/v1/envs/{env}/agents/{agent}` · scope `write` · MCP tool `agents_update`

Change an agent's fields. Lists you send (inputs, outputs, tools, projects, cards, items) replace the old ones. Moving it under one of its own reports is refused with reports_loop.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | string | yes | Environment id (see envs.list). |
| `agent` | string | yes | Agent id or name. |
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `kind` | enum |  | agent (AI agent), human, team, or automation (a scripted job without AI that runs on its own schedule outside Flow: no models, never live). One of `agent`, `human`, `team`, `automation`. |
| `title` | string |  | Role, e.g. Research. |
| `status` | enum |  | One of `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `retired`. |
| `live` | boolean |  | The switch runners obey: false (the default) and runners leave the agent alone; true and the runner named in runtime works its queue. |
| `reportsTo` | string |  | The agent it reports to: id or name; "" for top level. |
| `supervisor` | string |  | A person on a chart who oversees it: node id or name; "" for none. |
| `purpose` | string |  |  |
| `instructions` | string |  | System prompt or runbook. |
| `runtime` | string |  | Where it runs: a runner name from runners.list, e.g. a home server. |
| `models` | string[] |  | Model ids the runner reported (runners.list), in order: the primary first, then fallbacks it tries when one fails (or, with auto, the pool it picks from). Also sets model to the first. Wins over model when both are sent. |
| `model` | string |  | One model id, e.g. claudeAgent:claude-sonnet-5-5: the same as sending models with just it ("" for none). Always reads back as the first of models. |
| `auto` | boolean |  | false (the default): the runner starts on the first of models and falls back in order. true: models is a pool and the runner picks one per card. |
| `schedule` | string |  | When it runs, in plain words or cron, e.g. "Weekdays 09:00" (a note carried in the brief for an AI agent; the reference runner does not start work from it); "" for none. |
| `job` | union |  | The runner job it was promoted from: {runner, id} (see runners.report jobs); null or "" for none. |
| `inputs` | string[] |  | What it takes in. |
| `outputs` | string[] |  | What it produces. |
| `tools` | string[] |  | What it may use. |
| `projects` | string[] |  |  |
| `cards` | string | integer[] |  |  |
| `items` | string[] |  |  |
| `x` | number |  | Canvas position (with y). Leave out to place it under its manager. |
| `y` | number |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `agent.id` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.name` | string | yes |  |

| `agent.reportsTo` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.supervisor` | string | yes |  |
| `agent.purpose` | string |  |  |
| `agent.instructions` | string |  |  |
| `agent.runtime` | string |  |  |
| `agent.models` | string[] | yes |  |
